title: 第3章 兴家之子第4章 天赐家业
content_zh:
“娃…你…你真的成仙了？”
吴燃灯抬头，见吴老爹拄着拐杖，大伯、三叔还有吴小凡都站在那里，一个个伸长脖子往院里瞅，眼睛里满是惊惶和好奇。
他们一个个身上沾满了泥土，明明是冬雪初化的寒冷天气，却一个个满头大汗，分明是紧赶慢赶过来的，一个个心情急迫。
吴老爹等人又惊又怕。
镇上老人常说山里有精怪，可自家娃练出这等异状，是福是祸，一时间是惊喜，还是惊吓，他们都不知该如何是好了。
吴燃灯会心一笑，想来是吴小凡回去添油加醋说了墨池和暖屋的异状，才惊动了这一大家子。
吴老爹颤巍巍地迈进院门，目光先落在那方黑如浓墨的池水，又扫过满墙泛着微光的“福”字，最后定格在吴燃灯身上。
这孙儿明明还是那身洗旧的粗布衫，可眉宇间那股子沉静，却像是换了个人——先前是读书人的清苦，此刻竟透着种说不出的清气，连站在那里，都像是一幅恰好入了神韵的画，随时会飘然离去，捉不到，摸不着。
吴燃灯迎上去，扶稳爷爷的胳膊，指尖触到老人冰凉的手，便顺势将一丝刚学会的微弱灵气渡过去。
吴老爹只觉一股暖意从胳膊窜到心口，多年的老寒腿竟松快了些，瞪大眼睛说不出话。
“爷，大伯，三叔，”吴燃灯声音平和，“不是成仙，是入了‘道’。”
他指着墨池：“这水不是墨，是灵气凝的；这字也不是字，是引气的符。我前几日给你们写的信，说‘三年入道’，是真的。”
三叔咽了口唾沫，指着门上的“福”字：“那……这屋暖和，也是因为字？”
“是。”吴燃灯点头，“符道以字通灵，我练的，就是这个。”
吴老爹缓过神，忽然抓住他的手，掌心粗糙的茧子蹭着他指节的薄茧：“那…科举呢？你先前中了秀才，现在又入了道，还去考科举吗？”
显然吴老爹等人还是没有意识到，以字入道代表着什么。
科举功名，这才是一家人最上心的事。
吴燃灯望着爷爷眼里的期盼，又看了看大伯三叔紧张的神情，却是摇了摇头，轻叹道：“爷，世上的‘举’，可不止文举一种，还有一种只要踏入其中就能超凡脱俗的科举，称之为：‘仙举’。仙举得名，即为：仙士，从此不与凡俗混同，这才是孙儿的毕生之愿。”
青年话说得斩钉截铁，早已下定了决心。
他把从《仙举前尘录》里看到的事拣要紧的说了出来，“文举之上有仙举，考的不是文章，是修行。唯有入道者，才有资格应试。成者，脚踏青云，驻世长生。不成者，落于凡俗，百岁而枯……”

院里顿时一静，只有墨池的水在微风里轻晃。
吴老爹等人听到这等惊骇之语，一时为之失神。
“我就说你这娃从小心里就有大主意！但也没想不到你的心气这么高。”吴老爹盯着他看了半晌，忽然重重一叹，“文举之上还有仙举？这等惊世奇闻，岂是我这等老百姓所能知晓的？”
“也罢！不管这仙举是真是假，文举不考也罢。你能把破屋变福宅，能让池水变色，这本事，比当什么官都强哩！”
大伯愣了愣，也随即咧开嘴：“仙举？听着就比文举厉害！燃灯想考，家里砸锅卖铁也供！”
三叔也点头：“对！小凡，以后多来给你哥送东西，别让他缺了啥！”
吴燃灯望着一家人瞬间转变的神情，心里一暖。
他知道，这些话里有不懂，有盲从，却更有沉甸甸的信任。
“要考仙举，得先去郡城去仙塾求学，录得仙籍。”他轻声道，“我今日说这些，就是想告诉你们，我要走的路，和先前想的不一样了。”
吴老爹把烟锅子往鞋底磕了磕，重新点燃：“仙塾，仙籍？二伢子，你说的这些爷爷都不懂。但你选的路，准没错。啥时候走？家里给你收拾行囊！”
阳光穿过老宅的破窗，照在满墙的“福”字上，笔画间的灵气轻轻流转。
吴燃灯笑了，他知道，与之前全家齐心供他参加文举一样，这一次仙举，身后的家人，仍是他最稳的靠山。
content_en:
"Baby...you...are you really an immortal?"
Wu Randeng looked up and saw Father Wu leaning on a cane. His uncle, third uncle and Wu Xiaofan were all standing there, stretching their necks to look into the courtyard, their eyes full of panic and curiosity.
Each of them was covered with mud. It was obviously the cold weather when the winter snow had just melted, but they were all sweating profusely. They had obviously come here in a hurry, and they were all in a hurry.
Father Wu and others were shocked and frightened.
The old people in the town often say that there are spirits in the mountains, but their own child has developed such strange behavior. Whether it is a blessing or a curse, whether it is a surprise or a fright, they don't know what to do.
Wu Randeng smiled knowingly, thinking that it was Wu Xiaofan who went back and told the strange things about Mo Chi and Nuan Wu that he alerted the whole family.
Father Wu walked tremblingly into the courtyard door, his eyes first fell on the pool of water as black as thick ink, then scanned the shimmering word "福" on the wall, and finally settled on Wu Randeng.
The grandson is obviously still wearing the same old washed clothes, but the calmness between his brows seems to be a different person - he used to be a scholar, but now he is exuding an indescribable freshness. Even standing there, he looks like a painting that has just caught the charm, and will float away at any time, out of reach and out of touch.
Wu Randeng stepped forward to meet him, held his grandfather's arm steady, and when his fingertips touched the old man's cold hand, he transferred the faint spiritual energy he had just learned.
Father Wu felt a warmth rush from his arms to his heart. His legs, which had been cold for many years, relaxed a little faster. His eyes widened and he was speechless.
"Master, uncle, third uncle," Wu Randeng said in a calm voice, "It's not about becoming an immortal, it's about entering the Tao."
He pointed at the ink pool: "This water is not ink, it is condensed by spiritual energy; these words are not words, they are talismans for attracting Qi. The letter I wrote to you a few days ago, saying 'I entered Taoism in three years', is true."
The third uncle swallowed and pointed to the word "福" on the door: "Then... this room is warm, is it also because of the word "福"?"
"Yes." Wu Randeng nodded, "Fu Tao uses words to channel spirits. This is what I practice."
Father Wu calmed down and suddenly grabbed his hand, the rough calluses of his palm rubbing against the thin calluses of his knuckles: "What about... what about the imperial examination? You were a scholar before and now you have entered Taoism. Do you still want to take the imperial examination?"
Obviously, Father Wu and others still don't realize what it means to enter the Tao with words.
Imperial examination success is the most important thing for the family.
Wu Randeng looked at the expectation in his grandfather's eyes, and then at the nervous expression of his uncle and uncle, but he shook his head and sighed softly: "Master, there are more than just civil examinations in the world. There is also an imperial examination that can transcend the world as long as you step into it. It is called the 'immortal examination'. The name of the immortal examination means: immortal scholar. From now on, he will not be confused with the common people. This is the lifelong wish of his grandson."
The young man spoke firmly and had already made up his mind.
He summarized the important things he saw in "The Record of the Immortal Examination", "There is the Immortal Examination above the Literary Examination. The test is not about articles, but about practice. Only those who have entered the Taoism are qualified to take the exam. Those who succeed will have their feet on the blue clouds and live forever in this world. Those who fail will fall into the world and wither at the age of a hundred..."
The courtyard suddenly fell silent, with only the water in the ink pond swaying gently in the breeze.
When Father Wu and others heard these horrifying words, they were momentarily stunned.
"I told you that you have had big ideas since you were young! But I didn't expect you to be so ambitious." Father Wu stared at him for a long time, and suddenly sighed heavily, "There are immortal exams on top of the civil exams? How can ordinary people like me know such shocking anecdotes?"
"It doesn't matter! It doesn't matter whether this immortal test is true or not, it doesn't matter if you don't take the civil test. You can turn a dilapidated house into a blessed house and change the color of the pond. This ability is better than any official!"
The uncle was stunned for a moment, and then he grinned: "Xianju? It sounds better than the civil examination! If you want to take the exam, you can even smash pots and sell iron at home!"
The third uncle also nodded: "Yes! Xiaofan, come more often and give your brother things in the future. Don't let him lack anything!"
WuRan Deng felt warm in his heart as he watched the family's expressions change instantly.
He knew that there was some understanding and blind obedience in these words, but there was also a heavy trust in them.
"If you want to take the Immortal Examination, you must first go to the county to study in an Immortal School and obtain an Immortal Certificate." He said softly, "I am saying this today just to tell you that the path I want to take is different from what I thought before."
Father Wu knocked the cigarette pot against the sole of his shoe and lit it again: "Xianxue, Xianji? Eryaozi, grandpa doesn't understand what you are talking about. But the path you have chosen is definitely the right one. When are you leaving? I'll pack your bags at home!"
Sunlight passes through the broken windows of the old house and shines on the word "福" all over the wall, and the spiritual energy flows gently between the strokes.
Wu Randeng smiled. He knew that just like the previous time when his whole family worked together to support him in the literary examination, this time the family behind him would still be his most stable supporter.
